question.text: Post Finance (No.2) Act 2024 (w.e.f. 23 July 2024), what is the holding period for a security to be treated as LONG-TERM capital asset in the following cases?

answer.text: Listed equity: > 36 months; Unlisted equity: > 36 months; Listed debentures: > 36 months
Listed equity / equity-oriented MF units / listed debentures: > 12 months; Unlisted securities (incl. unlisted equity and LLP interest): > 24 months

explanation.text: The Logic: Finance (No.2) Act 2024, w.e.f. 23-07-2024, harmonised the LTC holding period: Listed securities (incl. units of UTI/equity-oriented MF, zero-coupon bonds, listed debentures) — > 12 months for LTC. Unlisted securities (unlisted equity, LLP interest) — > 24 months for LTC. Note: unlisted bonds/debentures transferred/redeemed on or after 23-07-2024 are DEEMED STC irrespective of holding period. The Trap: Option A is the pre-23-07-2024 regime for unlisted debentures. Option B over-simplifies. Option C is also outdated. Cross-Exam Context: XV, XXI-B, XIX-A all test holding periods; XIX-C expects manager to model exit timing around the bright-line. Manager's Pro-Tip: In exit modelling, cross the LTC bright-line. For unlisted equity, sell at 24m+1d (not 23m+29d) — a one-day miss flips rate from slab (could be 30%) to 12.5%. Build a calendar alert in the portfolio management system.
